identification.summary: Lemon Sandstorm is Microsoft's name for an Iran-origin threat actor formerly tracked by Microsoft as RUBIDIUM and also known as Pioneer Kitten [S1]. MITRE ATT&CK tracks it as Fox Kitten (G0117), describes a suspected nexus to the Iranian government, and reports activity since at least 2017 against entities in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia and North America [S2][S4]. Its signature is mass exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN and edge appliances, followed by hands-on intrusion with largely open-source and dual-use tools [S2][S5][S6][S11]. Microsoft implicated RUBIDIUM in the Pay2Key and N3tw0rm ransomware campaigns against Israel in late 2020 and early 2021 [S3]. An August 2024 FBI/CISA/DC3 advisory, as reported in the press, describes the same cluster selling or brokering network access to ransomware affiliates (ALPHV/BlackCat, NoEscape, RansomHouse) alongside separate espionage against Israel and Azerbaijan [S11][S12][S13]. Microsoft cites that warning in its October 2024 healthcare ransomware report [S14].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least 2017, per MITRE ATT&CK and CrowdStrike as summarized by MITRE [S2][S4], and per press coverage of the 2024 joint advisory [S12].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Lemon Sandstorm (formerly RUBIDIUM). Microsoft's naming feed lists RUBIDIUM and PIONEER KITTEN as other names [S1]. MITRE G0117 lists Fox Kitten, UNC757, Parisite, Pioneer Kitten, RUBIDIUM and Lemon Sandstorm [S2]. Press coverage of the 2024 advisory gives the same alias set and says the operators used the online handles 'Br0k3r' and, in 2024, 'xplfinder' [S11][S12]. Parisite is Dragos's name, and Dragos's reporting focuses on ICS-related targeting [S2][S10]. Vendor clusters overlap but are not guaranteed to be identical; see gaps.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft lists the actor's origin as Iran [S1]. Press coverage of the August 2024 FBI/CISA/DC3 advisory reports the FBI's assessment that the actors are associated with the Government of Iran and use the Iranian company name 'Danesh Novin Sahand' as a cover [S12][S13]. The sources gathered do not name a specific Iranian organization (for example IRGC or MOIS) as sponsor.
attribution.confidence: US government: the FBI assesses, per press reporting on the 2024 advisory, that the actors are associated with the Government of Iran [S12][S13]. CISA's 2020 alert, as cited by MITRE, described an 'Iran-based' actor [S6][S2]. Microsoft attributes Pay2Key and N3tw0rm to RUBIDIUM but publishes no confidence level [S3]. MITRE and CrowdStrike use 'suspected nexus' wording [S2][S4][S10]. Fortinet's incident responders, as reported by The Hacker News, tie a 2023-2025 Middle East intrusion to Lemon Sandstorm based on tradecraft overlaps [S15]. Morphisec, as reported by The Hacker News, assesses that Pay2Key.I2P is linked to Fox Kitten [S16]. None of the advisory texts were opened for this record.
attribution.basis: FBI/CISA/DC3 joint advisory (2024) as reported by Help Net Security, BleepingComputer and Infosecurity Magazine [S11][S12][S13]; Microsoft threat intelligence and naming [S1][S3][S14]; MITRE ATT&CK procedure mapping drawn from ClearSky, CrowdStrike, CISA, Check Point and Fortinet [S2][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9]; MISP galaxy [S10]; vendor reporting on 2025 activity [S15][S16].

objectives: Dual-track. (1) Espionage: gaining and maintaining access to entities holding information of likely intelligence interest to the Iranian government, per CrowdStrike as carried in MISP [S10]; ClearSky called the 2020 campaign 'espionage-offensive' [S5]. Press reporting on the 2024 advisory says the group also intrudes into organizations in Israel and Azerbaijan to steal sensitive technical data [S12][S13]. (2) Monetization and disruption: brokering access to ransomware affiliates for a share of ransom payments [S11][S12]; reporting on the advisory says the FBI viewed the 2020 Pay2Key campaign as an information operation against Israel-based infrastructure rather than a bid for ransom [S12]. In 2025, Pay2Key.I2P reportedly offered affiliates a higher profit share for attacks on Iran's enemies, including Israel and the US [S16].

sectors: ICS-related entities (per Dragos, as cited in MISP) [S10]
Middle East critical infrastructure (2023-2025 Fortinet case) [S9][S15]
targeting.notes: Targeting is opportunistic, driven by exposure of vulnerable internet-facing VPN, firewall and remote-access appliances, not by sector alone [S2][S6][S11]. US victims in the 2024 advisory coverage are mostly ransomware access targets; Israel and Azerbaijan are espionage targets [S12]. Sector list for 2017-2021 comes from MITRE [S2].

capabilities.summary: Initial access comes through n-day exploitation of edge devices. 2020 reporting covered Fortinet, Pulse Secure and Palo Alto VPNs [S2][S5][S6]. 2024 advisory coverage adds Citrix NetScaler, F5 BIG-IP, Ivanti, Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400) and Check Point gateways (CVE-2024-24919) [S11][S12]. In the 2023-2025 Fortinet case, initial access was via compromised SSL VPN credentials [S15]. Persistence relies on web shells (including China Chopper), scheduled tasks, newly created accounts and the sticky-keys backdoor [S2][S6][S11]. Tunneling and C2 use ngrok, SSHMinion, FRPC, Go Proxy, Plink and AWS-hosted C2, and MITRE associates SystemBC with the group [S2][S4][S6][S9]. The Fortinet case also featured custom malware: the HanifNet .NET backdoor, HXLibrary and NeoExpressRAT, plus MeshCentral. Fortinet reported at least five novel malware families [S15]. Credentials are dumped from LSASS, NTDS and KeePass [S2][S6]. Ransomware involvement spans the actor's own Pay2Key in 2020 [S7][S8], hands-on help to ALPHV/NoEscape/RansomHouse affiliates in encrypting victims [S11][S12], and the 2025 Pay2Key.I2P RaaS, which Morphisec reports is tied to Mimic ransomware capabilities [S16].

campaigns.name: Fox Kitten: widespread Iranian espionage-offensive campaign (ClearSky)
campaigns.summary: ClearSky reports a campaign that exploited known VPN vulnerabilities (Fortinet, Pulse Secure, Palo Alto) and remote services for initial access across multiple countries; MITRE uses this report as a core reference for the group.

campaigns.name: Who Is PIONEER KITTEN? (CrowdStrike)
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike profiles PIONEER KITTEN, including VPN exploitation and tunneling with ngrok and the custom SSHMinion tool.

campaigns.name: CISA AA20-259A: Iran-based actor exploits VPN vulnerabilities
campaigns.summary: CISA alert, as cited by MITRE, describes VPN exploitation followed by web shells, reverse proxies, credential dumping, and collection from shares, cloud storage and Microsoft Teams.

campaigns.name: Pay2Key ransomware campaign
campaigns.summary: Check Point (2020-11-06) and ClearSky (2020-12-17) report Pay2Key ransomware attacks; ClearSky attributes the campaign to Fox Kitten. Microsoft says RUBIDIUM was implicated in Pay2Key attacks targeting Israel.

campaigns.name: N3tw0rm ransomware campaign
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says RUBIDIUM was implicated in the N3tw0rm ransomware campaign that targeted Israel in late 2020 and early 2021.

campaigns.name: Long-term intrusion into Middle East critical infrastructure (FortiGuard IR)
campaigns.summary: Fortinet incident responders, as reported by The Hacker News, say an actor tied to Lemon Sandstorm held access for about two years. Initial access was through stolen SSL VPN credentials, followed by web shells, the HanifNet, HXLibrary and NeoExpressRAT backdoors, and attempted re-entry after containment.

campaigns.name: FBI/CISA/DC3 advisory: Iran-based actors enabling ransomware
campaigns.summary: Advisory, as reported, says the actors brokered access to US schools, municipalities, financial and healthcare organizations to ALPHV, NoEscape and RansomHouse affiliates. It also says they spied on targets in Israel and Azerbaijan and used the cover name Danesh Novin Sahand.

campaigns.name: Microsoft healthcare ransomware report cites Lemon Sandstorm
campaigns.summary: Microsoft notes the August 2024 US warning to the health sector about Lemon Sandstorm brokering access for ransomware gangs.

campaigns.name: Pay2Key.I2P ransomware-as-a-service
campaigns.summary: Morphisec, as reported by The Hacker News, links the revived Pay2Key.I2P RaaS to Fox Kitten. It reports more than 51 payouts and over $4M in four months, with an 80% affiliate share for attacks on Iran's enemies after the June 2025 Israel-Iran-US conflict.

diamond.adversary: Iran-origin actor that the FBI associates with the Government of Iran; cover company Danesh Novin Sahand; personas Br0k3r and xplfinder; Microsoft Lemon Sandstorm (formerly RUBIDIUM) [S1][S11][S12].
diamond.capability: N-day edge-device exploitation; web shells; tunneling tools (ngrok, FRPC, Plink, SSHMinion); SystemBC; custom backdoors HanifNet and NeoExpressRAT; credential dumping; Pay2Key and Pay2Key.I2P ransomware [S2][S4][S9][S12][S15][S16].
diamond.infrastructure: Reverse tunnels and proxies to actor C2, including ngrok and AWS-hosted servers [S2]; criminal-forum personas for access sales [S11][S12]; Keybase and Twitter for Pay2Key victim contact [S2][S7].
diamond.victim: US schools, municipalities, financial and healthcare organizations (access brokering); Israeli, Azerbaijani and UAE targets; Middle East critical infrastructure; historically oil and gas, defense and government in multiple regions [S2][S12][S15].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence collection for Iran [S10][S12] combined with revenue and pressure operations against Israel and the US, intensified after the June 2025 conflict [S3][S16].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing VPN, firewall and ADC appliances (Fortinet, Pulse/Ivanti, Palo Alto, Citrix, F5, Check Point); Windows AD; cloud and Teams collaboration data [S2][S6][S11][S12].

gaps: The 2024 FBI/CISA/DC3 advisory (IC3 PDF and CISA AA24-241A page) was not opened; its content is taken from press coverage [S11][S12][S13]. One search summary noted the IC3 PDF may carry a different product ID (AA24-233A); unverified.
Cover-company spelling varies in coverage ('Danesh Novin Sahand' vs 'Sahan'); confirm in the primary advisory [S13].

Older primary documents were not opened; their content comes from MITRE ATT&CK and MISP. These include CrowdStrike's PIONEER KITTEN profile, ClearSky's Fox Kitten and Pay2Kitten reports, CISA AA20-259A, Check Point's Pay2Key alert, the Fortinet 2025 report and Dragos PARISITE.

Fortinet's 2025 report itself was not opened. Its attribution wording and confidence, and the victim's identity, rest on The Hacker News coverage [S15]. A search summary of other coverage said the intrusion may trace to May 2021; unverified.
The Pay2Key.I2P attribution to Fox Kitten is Morphisec's assessment; no government confirmation was found [S16]. The links to Mimic ransomware and a reported Linux variant are unverified.
Some secondary sources (Truesec, Paubox) claim IRGC ties and a close link to Peach Sandstorm; these were not verified in primary reporting and are excluded.
Microsoft has no public dedicated Lemon Sandstorm profile; Microsoft coverage here is the naming feed, the 2021 MDDR blog and the 2024 healthcare report [S1][S3][S14].

Cluster boundaries: Parisite (Dragos), UNC757 (Mandiant) and Fox Kitten/Pioneer Kitten are mapped together by MITRE, MISP and the 2024 advisory coverage [S2][S10][S12]. Microsoft's own mapping lists only RUBIDIUM and PIONEER KITTEN [S1].
ICS targeting rests on MISP's summary of Dragos reporting; OT impact is unverified [S10].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Internet-facing VPN, firewall and ADC appliances (Fortinet, Ivanti/Pulse, Palo Alto, Citrix, F5, Check Point) are key cyber terrain [S2][S11][S12]. Victimology includes US municipal, education, finance and healthcare networks, Israeli, Azerbaijani and UAE targets, and Middle East critical infrastructure. These overlap with base support services, host nations and coalition partners [S12][S15]. STEP 2 (effects): Every new edge-device CVE widens the target set within days. Ransomware partnerships turn espionage access into availability effects [S11][S12]. STEP 3 (adversary template): n-day or stolen-credential VPN access; web shell or new account; tunnel (ngrok, FRPC, Plink, SystemBC) or custom backdoor (HanifNet, NeoExpressRAT); credential dumping; RDP/SMB movement; then data theft and/or a handoff to ransomware affiliates [S2][S6][S12][S15]. STEP 4: MLCOA is quiet, multi-year access for intelligence collection, with opportunistic access sales [S12][S15]. MDCOA is crisis-time activation of brokered or long-held access to encrypt or disrupt partner-nation critical infrastructure or DIB and installation-support networks, consistent with Pay2Key.I2P's pro-Iran affiliate incentives [S16]. Candidate indicators: exploitation of newly disclosed edge-device CVEs; new local or domain accounts after VPN logins from unfamiliar sources; scheduled tasks named like system services; outbound ngrok/FRP/MeshCentral traffic; VSS-based NTDS access; and forum offers of domain-admin access to sector peers [S2][S6][S12][S15].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: Track patch and compromise-assessment status of edge appliances across the DODIN, DIB and mission partners. The actor reuses stolen VPN credentials and persists after patching [S6][S15]. (2) Authorities: Activity blends state espionage with criminal ransomware [S12]. Incidents may need joint FBI, CISA and DC3 handling, and early clarity on lead agency, particularly for DIB and municipal or healthcare providers that support installations [S12][S14]. (3) Mission assurance: The Fortinet case shows two years of undetected dwell and attempted re-entry after eviction [S15]. Plan for credential resets, threat hunting and offline backups for mission-critical and ICS-adjacent systems. (4) Coordination: Share edge-exploitation and tunneling indicators with Israeli, Gulf and Azerbaijani partners and US critical-infrastructure sectors [S12]. Map vendor aliases (Pioneer Kitten, Fox Kitten, UNC757, Parisite, Br0k3r) so partner reporting links to one cluster [S1][S2][S11].

provenance.importedSummary: PIONEER KITTEN is an Iran-based adversary that has been active since at least 2017 and has a suspected nexus to the Iranian government. This adversary appears to be primarily focused on gaining and maintaining access to entities possessing sensitive information of likely intelligence interest to the Iranian government. According to DRAGOS, they also targeted ICS-related entities using known VPN vulnerabilities. They are widely known to use open source penetration testing tools for reconnaissance and to establish encrypted communications.
